newsitem.title: USA: BOTCC shareholders reject plan for CBOT directors.
newsitem.headline: BOTCC shareholders reject plan for CBOT directors.

text.p: The Board of Trade Clearing Corp (BOTCC) said Wednesday its shareholders rejected a proposal that would have allowed the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) to put two CBOT directors on the BOTCC board.
BOTCC is an independent clearing house for transactions made on CBOT and some other exchanges.
The proposal would have allowed the CBOT to nominate and elect two governors to the BOTCC board, the clearing house said.
Under the plan, the CBOT would have paid $330,000 to buy one BOTCC preferred share that would entitle the exchange to nominate the two governors, subject to BOTCC shareholder approval.
"We know this is an important issue to our shareholders as evidenced by the strong turnout of 115 votes," BOTCC chairman Christopher Hehmeyer said.

"We are pleased to say that one benefit from the past year's discussion on board representation has been increased coordination and cooperation between the Clearing Corporation and the Chicago Board of Trade," he added.
Of the total 115 votes cast, 48 were in favor of the proposal and 67 were opposed, BOTCC said.

BOTCC, founded in 1925, provides clearing and settlement services for contracts traded on CBOT and the MidAmerica Commodity Exchange. It also provides processing services to the New York Cotton Exchange and bookkeeping services to many futures market participants.
CBOT chairman Patrick Arbor said in a statement that he was disappointed by the vote. The proposal had been approved by the CBOT board of directors and BOTCC board of governors.
"As a result of this vote, I must bring the issue back to our Strategy Committee of Directors, as it raises certain strategic issues that must be addressed," he added.
He said the exchange had hoped for approval of the proposal, part of CBOT's 1997 strategic initiatives, to improve communication between the two organisations' governing boards.
